newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope prays for death-row man after letter plea.
newsitem.headline: Pope prays for death-row man after letter plea.

text.p: The Vatican said in a letter published on Sunday that Pope John Paul was praying for U.S. death-row prisoner Joseph O'Dell after he wrote an impassioned plea to the Pontiff care of an Italian newspaper.

"If I could make one more wish, it would be to feel the presence of his Holiness the Pope spiritually at my bedside at the moment when the executioner pushes the plunger of poison into my arm," O'Dell said in an undated letter sent to Italian daily La Repubblica.
"I pray that the Pope will pray for me, that he will find in his heart the forgiveness to pray for a wretched sinner like myself, like Jesus prayed for the robber on the cross."

The newspaper printed a response from the Vatican's Chief Spokesman, Joaquin Navarro-Valls, which noted the Pope had previously appealed for clemency on a humanitarian basis, and had seen O'Dell's letter. The Pope is on holiday in the Alps.
"The Pope would like to assure Mr O'Dell that he is always in his prayers, especially at this time," Navarro-Valls said.
"And he reminds everyone, once more, that only the Lord is master of life and death." Navarro-Valls confirmed the contents of the letter to reporters in the Alpine town of Les Combes.
O'Dell is sentenced to die on July 23 following a decision last month by the U.S. Supreme Court to uphold a death sentence imposed in 1986, when he was found guilty of killing a woman.

The state of Virginia had scheduled his execution for last December but the Court blocked the sentence at the last minute after a storm of protest, especially from Italy, where the Pope and Prime Minister Romano Prodi led pleas for clemency.

Italy, which has no death penalty in civilian criminal cases, is among the most vociferous advocates of a worldwide abolition of capital punishment and Italians have staged street protests to call for a reprieve for O'Dell.
"My execution is but a few days away," O'Dell said. "An unjust death is upon me...if I die by lethal injection on Wednesday July 23, I will die an innocent man."
O'Dell thanked the Italian people and the "extraordinary kindness and mercifulness" of the Pope.

"I've committed awful acts in my wretched life," he said. "I've done things for which I had to do just time behind bars. But one thing I have not done: I have not killed the poor woman whose blood is on the hands of someone walking free in America."

O'Dell slammed his trial, saying the evidence was "botched, misread and mishandled" and saying the star witness against him had recanted his testimony and admitted he lied. He said he had been prevented from having a new trial on "a technicality".
The Supreme Court, by a 5-4 vote, rejected claims that the sentence should be overturned, although O'Dell can appeal to the governor of Virginia.
La Repubblica published a statement from Prodi reaffirming Italy's opposition to the death penalty and describing O'Dell's case as "particularly harrowing".
